issues.body: The test only rejects a parsed value exactly equal to Python True. A workflow edit such as `continue-on-error: ${{ true }}` is parsed by PyYAML as a string and therefore passes this assertion while enabling failure swallowing in GitHub Actions. This leaves a bypass in the structural regression guard's load-bearing invariant, although the workflow in this PR does not use such a form.
issues.fix_hint: Require both the job and fmt-step values to be absent or exactly false, as the repository's arm-capability wiring test already does (for example, assert the value is in `(None, False)`).
issues.title: continue-on-error guard accepts non-boolean enabling forms

verdict.summary: The change correctly converts the existing rustfmt step into a hard gate, updates the associated documentation, and applies a workspace-wide mechanical rustfmt normalization. The new posture test exercises the intended current configuration and is wired into the existing quick-gates job after its shared PyYAML setup. One minor robustness gap remains in the regression test: expression/string forms of continue-on-error could evade its boolean-only assertion, though the checked-in workflow itself is correctly gating.
